title: Finite product decomposition of coefficient intersection scalars
statement: Let f:X -> T be separated [def-pc-morphism-conventions], U an affine open of T, Z an affine open of Y=f inverse image U, and g:Tprime -> U, gprime:Xprime -> X, fprime:Xprime -> Tprime a cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product] with f and g followed by U. Let V=Y.ι(Z), W=gprime inverse image V, B an affine open of Tprime, and I=W intersect fprime inverse image B. For every a in Gamma(Xprime,I,O), there are n, r_j in Gamma(Tprime,B,O), and d_j in Gamma(X,V,O), for j in Fin n, such that a=sum_j rho(r_j)*delta(d_j). Here rho is fprime.app B followed by restriction to I, and delta is gprime.app V followed by restriction to I. No module sheaf is involved.

source.place: Tag 02KG, Lemma 30.5.1, affine tensor computation in the proof

proof.text: V is affine by IsAffineOpen.image_of_isOpenImmersion applied to Z and Y.ι. Also V is contained in f inverse image U, B is contained in (g composed with U.ι) inverse image U, and I is the intersection of the inverse images of V and B. Mathlib isIso_pushoutSection_of_isAffineOpen applied to the original square and U,V,B, followed by isIso_pushoutSection_iff, gives the categorical ring pushout of Gamma(X,V) and Gamma(Tprime,B) over Gamma(T,U).

Give the two factor rings their algebras via the explicit appLE maps. Compare the pushout with CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct, using isoIsPushout on the flipped square. The two projection identities prove that the resulting isomorphism sends r tensor 1 to rho(r) and 1 tensor d to delta(d). Multiplicativity proves the product formula on r tensor d.

Apply TensorProduct.exists_sum_tmul_eq to the inverse image of a under the constructed isomorphism. Apply the forward map to its finite sum identity, use its inverse identity and map_sum, then replace each pure tensor by the product formula. Unfold appLE to obtain exactly the two displayed restriction maps. All maps and isomorphisms are constructed from universal properties; there is no arbitrary witness from an unproved existence theorem. The empty sum covers zero; empty affine opens and zero rings are allowed throughout.

proof_origin.place: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02KG, affine tensor computation; implemented via Mathlib affine pushout sections and tensor finite sums

lean.statement:
theorem coefficientIntersection_scalar_decomposition
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T) [IsSeparated f]
    (U : T.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (Z : (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.Opens) (hZ : IsAffineOpen Z)
    {T' X' : Scheme.{u}} (g : T' ⟶ U.toScheme) (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f (g ≫ U.ι))
    (W : X'.Opens) (hW : W = g' ⁻¹ᵁ ((f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ''ᵁ Z))
    (B : T'.Opens) (hB : IsAffineOpen B)
    (a : Γ(X', W ⊓ f' ⁻¹ᵁ B)) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (r : Fin n → Γ(T', B))
      (d : Fin n → Γ(X, (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ''ᵁ Z)),
      a = ∑ j, (X'.presheaf.map (homOfLE
        (inf_le_right : W ⊓ f' ⁻¹ᵁ B ≤ f' ⁻¹ᵁ B)).op (f'.app B (r j))) *
        (X'.presheaf.map (homOfLE (show
          W ⊓ f' ⁻¹ᵁ B ≤ g' ⁻¹ᵁ ((f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ''ᵁ Z) from
            inf_le_left.trans hW.le)).op
          (g'.app ((f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ''ᵁ Z) (d j)))
